title: Half-block pixel renderer and Cento terminal component
goal: Render Cento's pixel animations in the terminal with the half-block technique at every colour tier, exposed as an Ink `<Cento>` component that respects frame durations, redraw budgets and the ASCII fallback.
scope_in: Half-block renderer `renderHalfBlock(rows, palette, opts)` ported from assets/mascot/play.py: two vertical pixels per cell, `▀` with fg = top and bg = bottom, `▄` when only the bottom pixel is set, space when empty; odd row counts padded with a transparent row.
Recolour support for the five Cento colours using the `palmap` and friend characters (`1`,`2`,`3`) in animations.json (violet, red, yellow, green, brown) so a crowd scene can mix colours.
Tier handling: truecolor 38;2/48;2 sequences, xterm-256 via `toXterm256` (lane C032) for tier 256, ASCII fallback for tier 16 and none or `unicode:false`.

ASCII Cento fallback (DESIGN §19.3): antenna `¡` line then face, frames idle `(•_•)`, happy `(^_^)`, thinking `(•_•?)`, error `(x_x)`, sleeping `(-_-)zZ`, working `(•_•)⌨`; ASCII-only variants `(o_o)` when unicode is off.

`<Cento animation color size playing onDone />` Ink component with a frame clock honouring each frame's `d` ms (80-500 ms), a per-animation frame cache of rendered ANSI strings, and lazy loading of animations.json by category from packages/mascot (lane C009).

Sizes: `hero` = full animation canvas (body 12x12 = 6 rows x 12 cols; canvases up to 14x15 px = 8 rows x 14 cols with props) and `mini` = 2 rows x 6 cols (DESIGN §3.7) produced by 2x box downsample of the body region only.
scope_out: Choosing which animation plays for which state, dwell, caps and priorities (lane C046).
Where the mascot is placed in layouts (callers in lanes C034, C036, C048).
Reduced-motion substitution logic (lane C049 sets a `motion` context this component reads).
Creating or editing animation data (assets/mascot is the source of truth; lane C009 packages it).
build_against: animations.json and `palmap` from assets/mascot via packages/mascot (lane C009); Python reference output from `python3 assets/mascot/play.py <name>` captured once into golden files under packages/tui/test/golden/pixel/.
interfaces: `renderHalfBlock(rows: string[], palette: Record<string,[number,number,number]>, opts: {tier: ColorTier; recolor?: (ch: string) => string}): string[]`
`<Cento animation: string; color?: CentoColor; size?: CentoSize; playing?: boolean; loop?: boolean; onDone?: () => void />`
`createFrameCache(loader: AnimationLoader): { lines(animation: string, frame: number, color: CentoColor, tier: ColorTier): string[] }`
acceptance: For 10 animations (`idle_breathe`, `thinking`, `error`, `celebrate`, `sleeping`, `reading_file`, `permission_prompt`, `tests_passing`, `crash`, `first_run_welcome`) the truecolor output is byte-identical to the Python `play.py` render for frame 0 and the last frame (golden files).
`idle_breathe` renders to 8 rows x 14 columns (canvas 14x15 px) and the Cento body occupies 6 rows x 12 columns; the `mini` size renders in exactly 2 rows x 6 columns.
Tier 256 output contains no `38;2` sequences; tier 16 and none output contains no ANSI colour sequences and uses `asciiCento`.
Frame advance honours each frame's `d`: with a fake clock, a 450 ms frame stays 450 ms (+/-10 ms) and the component never re-renders faster than the current frame's duration.
Rendering one frame from cache takes under 2 ms at p95 on the CI runner over 1,000 iterations (DESIGN §19.6 budget); the first uncached render is allowed 10 ms.
At most 6 `<Cento>` components animate concurrently; the 7th and later hold on their first frame until a slot frees (enforced by a shared `AnimationBudget`).
`playing={false}` or the motion context `reduced` renders a single static frame (the last frame for one-shots, frame 0 for loops) and starts no timers.
Unmounting clears the timer and leaves no pending callbacks (leak test).
tests: pixel/golden.test.ts: byte comparison with play.py renders.
pixel/clock.test.ts: frame timing, cache hits, unmount cleanup.
pixel/budget.test.ts: concurrent animation cap of 6; render time benchmark guard.
pixel/recolor.test.ts: five colours and mixed crowd friend chars.
guardrails: MUST NOT draw the mascot inside tool results, diffs or code blocks (DESIGN §10.1.9); the component refuses to render when a `noMascot` context flag is set by those containers.
MUST NOT redraw faster than the frame duration and MUST NOT clear the whole screen; update only the component's own rows (Ink diffing) per DESIGN §19.3.
MUST NOT add pixels, highlights or colours to the sprites; render exactly what animations.json defines (DESIGN §3.4).
MUST NOT block the render loop: animation JSON is loaded lazily by category and parsing happens once, off the hot path.
MUST treat an unknown animation name as `idle_breathe` and log once at debug; never throw during render.
Antenna tip mint (`glow-400`) and body colours MUST come from the animation palette even when the status colours use ANSI names (brand moment).
failure_modes: animations.json fails to load -> render the ASCII fallback for the requested state and log once at warn.
Terminal narrower than the sprite (cols < 14) -> render nothing (caller should already have hidden it via `mascotAllowed`).
notes: The `mini` 2x6 size in DESIGN §3.7 has no dedicated sprite set in animations.json; this card produces it by box downsampling the 12x12 body. If design wants hand-drawn mini sprites, that is a new asset task. Palette keys beyond B D H S T P are in `DATA['palette']`.
